Zhu Tóupí’s 30th Anniversary Reflections

Veteran Taiwanese singer Zhu Tóupí discusses his upcoming gratitude concert on June 26 at Taipei’s Huashan Legacy, celebrating three decades in music. He recounts his early days participating in student movements and leading the New Taiwanese Folk Song movement, which broadened Taiwan’s musical diversity. Zhu emphasizes that the freedom he enjoys on stage is built on the sacrifices of democratic pioneers, and he remains committed to opening doors for younger artists.

58th Golden Bell Awards Highlight

At the 58th Golden Bell Awards in Taipei, Zhu Tou-Pi accepted the Lifestyle Program Host Award for his work on "Listen! Taiwan is Singing." Dressed in a light blue suit and checkered shirt, he stood confidently on stage as the audience applauded his achievement. The ceremony, organized over two days to separate program and drama categories, saw Formosa Television (FTV) secure multiple honors.

Jutoupi: Pioneer of Taiwanese Hip-Hop

Jutoupi, born 朱約信 and known by his stage name 朱頭皮, is celebrated as Taiwan’s first rapper to fuse local language and identity into hip-hop. The image shows him on stage with a guitar, wearing a straw hat and glasses, backed by band members in soft focus. Bold yellow Chinese text reads “台灣嘻哈先河” and “豬頭皮 / 朱約信,” while an English newspaper excerpt by Glenn Smith highlights his debut album “Wo hish Shenjingbing” and its translation “I Am Insane.”
